title: My roguelite was built with Claude Code and is tested by a headless AI player that plays it by itself
author: Tommyruin
selftext:
Two kinds of AI in one game: Claude Code writes the code, and a rules-based AI player (it scores moves with tunable weights; no neural network) plays full runs against the same rules engine the players use, so broken Blessings and dead ends show up as numbers before players find them. It's really helped to balance out progression pathways and power levels of blessings prior to launch!

**Aita: The Dark Domain**, is a roguelite played with a normal deck of playing cards in the Etruscan underworld. Every card you attack with is a card you no longer have when the enemy hits back. Solo or online co-op for 1–4 players. Out 1 December on Steam, Google Play and the App Store for £1.99 / $1.99, with a [free demo on Steam now](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4730130/?utm_source=reddit&utm_campaign=full_release_2026&utm_content=built_with_claude).

Here's what I found made it work:

\- One rules engine. Every card, Blessing and boss rule lives in one shared core that solo, co-op, the game server and the test player all run. A rule written anywhere else counts as a bug, and parity tests check that solo, co-op and the server reach the same result.

\- A good .md file that every session reads first (naming, architecture, what "done" means), plus handoff notes so the next session starts where the last one ended.

\- Gates before every push: lint, tests, a build, a docs check and a translation check. The game is in 14 languages, and the check fails if one is out of date.

\- The headless AI player as previously mentioned. Building this was huge, and i'm consistently iterating on it to ensure a good power curve and difficulty level

Early on, rules lived inside the each mode separately, so solo and co-op could drift apart. In Feb I pulled every rule into one shared core *(or at least thought so, I kept finding small bits that lived outside the core until October!).* Additionally, the games were built two different ways until I moved every one of them onto a single pixel canvas in October - this was a huge visual upgrade.

I feel like with a coding background, these mistakes would have been removed from the word go, but unfortunately it was a lesson I had to learn along the way. At least I wont make it in my next projects!!

Numbers: 1,644 commits since 5 January, 943 with a Claude co-author line (57%), about 172k lines of game code (not counting my marketing tools) and 135k lines of tests. I switched around based on what was flavour of the month subscription wise, and I got married in June, hence the slow down! I'm sure a few hundred more to go before the 1st December!

Please [Try the demo here](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4730130/?utm_source=reddit&utm_campaign=full_release_2026&utm_content=built_with_claude) and give it a Wishlist!!!

Happy to answer any questions! :)
